newsitem.title: USA: Intermet to meet or beat Q4 estimates- CEO.
newsitem.headline: Intermet to meet or beat Q4 estimates- CEO.

text.p: Intermet Corp Chief Executive Officer John Doddridge said Tuesday Intermet expects to meet or exceed analysts fourth quarter earnings estimates despite strikes at General Motors Corp and expenses from Intermet's planned $12.50 a share tender offer for Sudbury Inc.
Doddridge, in a conference call, did not provide a range. First Call showed fourth quarter estimates of $0.28-$0.31 a share. The foundry company earned $0.24 in the 1995 quarter.
Strikes and merger-related expenses will hurt earnings, but income tax reductions in the form of reduced tax valuation allowances are expected, said Doddridge, who is also chairman.

Doddridge had cautioned last month GM's Canada strike would hurt Intermet's fourth quarter. Tuesday he said the impact of that and work stoppages at some U.S. GM plants is not yet tallied but will probably be "a couple cents for the fourth quarter."
Tuesday he said, "The effect of the strikes plus ... expenses associated with the (merger) ... will put us at the lower end of the analysts' expectations.
"But we believe at this time that the tax reduction we expect to have ... will take us up to the high (end of the) range, maybe out of the high range," he said.
